title: Build Hour: Valuemaxxing with GPT-5.6
description:
Get more useful work from every token with GPT-5.6. In this Build Hour, you’ll learn how to choose the right model for your workload, and migrate production agents while improving speed, cost, and performance.

Charlie Guo (DevEx), Bryant Chou (Founder, Ploy) and Lorenzo Gentile (AI Engineer, Ploy) will cover how to:

• Choose between GPT-5.6 Sol, Terra, and Luna based on intelligence, latency, and cost
• Measure and optimize cost-performance across real workloads
• Adapt evals, agent harnesses, tool schemas, and prompt caching when migrating models
• Move production agents to GPT-5.6, featuring a customer spotlight on how Ploy achieved 2.2× faster builds at 27% lower cost
• Apply these lessons through live demos and Q&A

segments.heading: Core Architecture and Technical Motivations for Build Hour: Valuemaxxing with GPT-5.6
segments.text: In this session on Build Hour: Valuemaxxing with GPT-5.6, OpenAI Developer Platform Team examine the underlying architectural principles and operational requirements shaping frontier AI systems. The presentation highlights how modern engineering teams leverage OpenAI, GPT-5.6, Token Optimization to address foundational challenges in LLM Fundamentals, Prompt Engineering, Product/Startup. Rather than relying on rigid heuristic pipelines, the architecture emphasizes end-to-end model legibility, structured context windows, and robust feedback loops. Participants explore how these patterns eliminate brittle manual glue code, providing a resilient platform capable of maintaining accuracy even under intense compute constraints and rapid requirement iteration.

segments.heading: Implementation Mechanics, System Workflows, and Tool Integrations
segments.text: Diving into technical mechanics, the speakers demonstrate concrete implementation workflows using OpenAI, GPT-5.6, Token Optimization. Key engineering workflows center on deterministic execution pipelines, rigorous schema validation, and low-latency data flow. By decomposing complex objectives into auditable intermediate states, developers can reliably track token expenditures, isolate runtime anomalies, and enforce strict execution boundaries. The session walks through hands-on architectures where automated orchestration safely manages high-concurrency requests, external API calls, and persistent state stores.

segments.heading: Operational Deployment, Evaluation Benchmarks, and Future Trajectory
segments.text: The concluding segment addresses enterprise deployment standards, cost efficiency trade-offs, and empirical evaluation benchmarks. Speakers present metrics for assessing reliability in production environments, emphasizing continuous evaluation against realistic task distributions. Organizations deploying OpenAI, GPT-5.6, Token Optimization must balance inference latency with reasoning depth, ensuring that guardrails and safety invariants remain intact throughout system lifecycle. Looking ahead, the discussion outlines upcoming platform milestones and strategic paradigms for scaling autonomous, high-integrity AI workloads across diverse industry domains.
